title.justification: The paper primarily focuses on analyzing idioms using computational methods, exploring their conventionality and contingency.
title.quote: Idioms are unlike most phrases in two im-portant ways. First, words in an idiom have non-canonical meanings. Second, the non-canonical meanings of words in an idiom are contingent on the presence of other words in the idiom.

extractions.description: This paper explores the nature of idioms, particularly focusing on their non-canonical meanings and how these meanings depend on the combination of words. The paper defines two measures: conventionality and contingency, and implements them using BERT and XLNet. It suggests that idioms do not require special linguistic machinery and highlights asymmetries in idiomatic phrases. The study primarily concerns language understanding and has no direct focus on sustainable development.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper does not address issues related to climate or ecological sustainable development; its focus is on linguistic theories and computational analyses of idioms.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This paper presents evidence that prototypical idioms occupy a particular region of the space of these two mechanisms, but are not otherwise ex-ceptional.

primary_category.justification: The paper is centered on linguistic analysis and computational methods for understanding idioms, which does not align with any sustainable development categories related to climate or ecology.
primary_category.quote: Our idiom dataset consists of phrases that have at some point been called idioms in the linguistics literature.

primary_sub_category.justification: As the primary category is 'N/A', the sub-category does not apply. The research does not pertain to any ecological or climate-related sub-categories.
primary_sub_category.quote: We define two measures, conventionality—meant to measure the degree to which words are interpreted in a canonical way, and contin-gency—a statistical association measure meant to capture the degree to which the presence of one word form depends on the presence of another.

new_primary_category.justification: No new sustainable development category applies as the research topic is unrelated to sustainable development themes.
new_primary_category.quote: What does seem clear is that pro-totypical cases of idiomatic phrases tend to have higher levels of both non-conventional meaning and contingency between words.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not introduce any new sustainable development concepts or categories that would fit within the existing framework of climate or ecological sustainability.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our conventionality measure is built on the idea that a word being used in a conventional way should have similar or related meanings across contexts, whereas a non-conventional word mean-ing can be idiosyncratic to particular contexts.
